title: Database Indexing Strategies
description: A team has a composite B-tree on (tenant_id, created_at), then proposes more indexes for a write-heavy table. Which statement is a sound starting point before checking EXPLAIN?

options.text: Adding more indexes always improves query performance
options.explanation: Indexes can speed matching reads but add storage and maintenance work. Inserts add entries, and updates or deletes may require index work; not every update changes every index. Unused indexes can hurt a write-heavy workload.

options.text: A compound index on (A, B) naturally supports A or (A, B) lookups; B-only queries are generally a poorer fit
options.explanation: Keys are sorted by A first and B within each A value, so a B-only predicate usually cannot seek as directly. Engine-specific skip scans and planner strategies are exceptions; inspect EXPLAIN rather than treating this as a prohibition.

options.text: B-tree indexes are ideal for full-text search
options.explanation: B-tree indexes are optimized for equality and range queries. Full-text search requires inverted indexes (like those in Elasticsearch or PostgreSQL's GIN indexes).

options.text: Covering indexes are indexes that span all tables in a database
options.explanation: A covering index includes the values needed for a particular query. It can allow an index-only scan, but visibility checks and engine behavior may still require table access.
